'''Wilhelmina Luten Seccombe Riley''' (September 30, 1906 –  October 1986) was an American statistician associated with federal government programs including the [[Works Progress Administration]], the [[Economic Cooperation Administration]], the [[Mutual Security Agency]], and the [[United States Agency for International Development|Agency for International Development]] (USAID).

==Early life and education==
Luten was born in [[Indiana]], the daughter of Daniel Benjamin Luten and Edith Heath Hull Luten.<ref>{{Cite book |url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/The_Indianapolis_Society_Blue_Book_Conta/NtMWAQAAMAAJ?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=Wilhelmina%20Luten&pg=PA38&printsec=frontcover |title=The Indianapolis Society Blue Book, Containing the Names and Addresses of Prominent Residents Arranged Alphabetically and by Street, Also Summer Residents, Ladies' Maiden Names, Club Membership, and Other Valuable Social Information |date=1924 |publisher=Blue Books Company |pages=38 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=1965-03-11 |title=Obituary for Edith Luten |via=Newspapers.com |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/journal-and-courier-obituary-for-edith-l/206307724/ |access-date=2026-09-19 |work=Journal and Courier |pages=8}}</ref> Her father was a math and engineering instructor at the [[University of Michigan]] and [[Purdue University]].<ref>{{Cite book |last=Purdue University |url=http://archive.org/details/debris001898purd |title=Debris |date=1890 |publisher=Indianapolis, Ind. : Press of Baker & Randolph |others=Allen County Public Library Genealogy Center}}</ref> She graduated from [[Shortridge High School]] in 1923,<ref>{{Cite news |date=1927-06-04 |title=Wins Contest |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-indianapolis-star-wins-contest/206304287/ |access-date=2026-09-19 |work=The Indianapolis Star |pages=4 |via=Newspapers.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=1923-09-29 |title=Six Shortridge Graduates Pass Entrance Examinations for Eastern Universities |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-indianapolis-news-six-shortridge-gra/206322106/ |access-date=2026-09-20 |work=The Indianapolis News |pages=20 |via=Newspapers.com}}</ref> and from [[Smith College]] in 1927,<ref>{{Cite news |date=1927-06-04 |title=Women Prominent in Society of Indianapolis |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-indianapolis-news-women-prominent-in/206303328/ |access-date=2026-09-19 |work=The Indianapolis News |via=Newspapers.com|pages=23}}</ref><ref>Smith College, [https://archive.org/details/class1927smit/page/74/mode/1up?q=Wilhelmina+Luten ''Class of 1927''] (1927 yearbook): 74; via Internet Archive.</ref> with graduate studies at [[Simmons University|Simmons College]].<ref>{{Cite book |last=Simmons College (Boston, Mass.) |first= |url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/Catalogue/w4jOAAAAMAAJ?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=Wilhelmina%20Luten&pg=RA3-PA36&printsec=frontcover |title=Catalogue |date=1928 |publisher=The College. |pages=36 |language=en}}</ref>

==Career==
Luten was a summer camp counselor after college,<ref>{{Cite journal |date=July 1929 |title=Class Notes: 1927 |url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/The_Smith_Alumnae_Quarterly/tcPOAAAAMAAJ?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=Wilhelmina%20Luten&pg=PA556&printsec=frontcover |journal=Smith Alumnae Quarterly |volume=20 |issue=4 |pages=556}}</ref> and a fellow in the research department of the [[Women's Educational and Industrial Union]] in Boston.<ref name=":1">{{Cite journal |last=Luten |first=Wilhelmina |date=1929 |title=Unemployment as a Cause of Family Dependency |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/41813832 |journal=Monthly Labor Review |publisher=Bureau of Labor Statistics, U.S. Department of Labor |volume=29 |issue=6 |pages=1–12 |issn=0098-1818}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=Women's Educational and Industrial Union (Boston, Mass.) |first= |url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/Annual_Report_of_the_Women_s_Educational/xqk2AAAAMAAJ?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=Wilhelmina%20Luten&pg=PA15&printsec=frontcover |title=Annual Report of the Women's Educational and Industrial Union |date=1928 |publisher=Women's Educational and Industrial Union. |pages=15 |language=en}}</ref> In 1932 she was statistician for the Detroit Department of Public Welfare.<ref name=":4" /> In 1934 she was named supervisor of the [[Federal Emergency Relief Administration]]'s field office in Louisiana.<ref>{{Cite news |date=1934-06-29 |title=Lake Charles is One of 79 FERA Research Points |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/american-press-lake-charles-is-one-of-79/206304548/ |access-date=2026-09-19 |work=American Press |pages=15 |via=Newspapers.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=1934-06-28 |title=Survey Relief Clients; ERA Unit Makes Survey of Occupations of Clients |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/american-press-survey-relief-clients-er/206304787/ |access-date=2026-09-19 |work=American Press |pages=1 |via=Newspapers.com}}</ref> She prepared reports on employment for the Works Progress Administration in the 1930s.<ref name=":2" /><ref>{{Cite book |url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/Directory_of_Statisticians_of_the_United/wXNQBXcd95cC?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=Wilhelmina%20Luten&pg=RA1-PA141&printsec=frontcover |title=Directory of Statisticians of the United States Government |date=1941 |pages=141 |language=en}}</ref> She was an analytical statistician at the Economic Cooperation Administration in the 1940s, and for the Mutual Security Agency<ref>{{Cite book |url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/Statistical_Reporter/mwaiwVAzjzgC?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=Wilhelmina%20Luten&pg=PA105&printsec=frontcover |title=Statistical Reporter |date=May 1953 |publisher=Division of Statistical Standards, Bureau of the Budget |pages=105 |language=en}}</ref> and the Agency for International Development (USAID).<ref name=":3" />

==Publications==
* "Unemployment as a cause of family dependency" (1929)<ref name=":1" />
* "A Survey of 1200 Families, Detroit Department of Public Welfare" (1932)<ref name=":4">{{Cite journal |last=Luten |first=Wilhelmina |date=June 1932 |title=A Survey of 1200 Families, Detroit Department of Public Welfare |url=https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/104438943201300406 |journal=The Family |language=en |volume=13 |issue=4 |pages=127–130 |doi=10.1177/104438943201300406 |issn=0887-400X}}</ref>
* ''An analysis of employment of women on Works Progress Administration projects, December 1935 through May 1936'' (1936, WPA report)<ref name=":2">{{Cite book |last=Luten |first=Wilhelmina. |url=https://catalog.hathitrust.org/Record/102193289 |title=An analysis of employment of women on Works Progress Administration projects, December 1935 through May 1936 |date=1936 |publisher=Works Progress Administration, Division of Research, Statistics, and Records }}</ref>

==Personal life==
Luten married twice. She married William T. Seccombe in 1949;<ref>{{Cite news |date=1949-11-27 |title=Marriage License Applications |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/evening-star-marriage-license-applicatio/206305070/ |access-date=2026-09-19 |work=Evening star |pages=22 |via=Newspapers.com}}</ref> he died in 1961.<ref>{{Cite news |date=1961-02-20 |title=Obituary for William Seccombe |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/evening-star-obituary-for-william-seccom/206304930/ |access-date=2026-09-19 |work=Evening star |pages=28 |via=Newspapers.com}}</ref> Her second husband was fellow statistician Donald C. Riley; he died in 1973.<ref>{{Cite news |date=1973-04-29 |title=Donald C. Riley Is Dead; Ex‐Statistical Official, 68 |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1973/04/29/archives/donald-c-riley-is-dead-exstatistical-official-68.html |access-date=2026-09-19 |work=The New York Times |pages=61 |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref> She died in 1986, at the age of 80, at a hospital in northern Virginia.<ref name=":3">{{Cite news |date=October 9, 1986 |title=Wilhelmina Luten Seccombe Riley, 80 |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/archive/local/1986/10/09/368ef612-3d9c-4253-85b5-e12a8fb42506/ |work=Washington Post}}</ref>
